question.problem:
Given that ${\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x=5$ and ${\int }_{2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-1,$ 
then what is ${\int }_{0}^{6}(4-5f(x))\,\text{d}x?$

${\int }_{0}^{6}(4-5f(x))\,\text{d}x=$ 
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
From the adjacent intervals rule, we know that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,{\int }_{2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,=\,{\int }_{0}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Plugging in the known information gives

$$
5+(-1)\,=\,{\int }_{0}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,⇒\,{\int }_{0}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=4.
$$

Finally, compute the desired integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{6}(4-5f(x))\,\text{d}x & =4{\int }_{0}^{6}1\,\text{d}x\,-\,5{\int }_{0}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\cdot x{|}_{0}^{6}\,-\,5(4) \\  & =4(6-0)-20 \\  & =24-20 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
